role.altitude: The analysts stop pulling AFAS extracts into Excel and checking manager spreadsheets cell by cell. They own the cost drivers, allocation keys, budget rules and the forecast logic. They spend their week on cause, options and conversations with site managers, the Finance Director and the bank.
reach: Controller: month-close reconciliations and accrual checks. Learn how journal timing affects the variance tables.
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: headcount and flex-hour data in AFAS. Learn the FTE and absence definitions behind labour cost drivers.
Bookkeeper: agency invoice matching. Learn which mismatches between hours and invoices show up as cost overruns.
Finance Director: board and bank packs. Learn which forecast questions the board asks, so the drivers answer them.
skills_to_grow: Driver-based planning: volume, shifts, flex hours, fuel and rent as defined drivers per site
Power BI semantic modelling and DAX, enough to own the certified finance model
Writing check rules and allocation keys as versioned code or config that the auditor can rebuild
Reviewing model-drafted commentary for numbers that do not tie
Advising managers with options and trade-offs, not one answer
role.ambitious_version: A monthly rolling forecast for each site (Rotterdam, Tilburg, Venlo) with three scenarios for flex demand and volume, built from defined drivers on a certified Power BI model. Site managers get a short commentary each month and the board gets a forecast it trusts within days of close.

tasks.short: Advise managers on cost analysis, allocations and budget preparation using AFAS data pulled into Excel.

steps.what: Take the manager's question and pull actuals from AFAS and Power BI into Excel
Build the cost analysis or allocation by cost centre and site
Write a short memo with options and their cost effect

loop.input: cost analysis tables and the manager question
loop.output: draft memo with two or three options, each tied to table figures
loop.check: every number in the text is matched by code against the analysis table; mismatch blocks the draft
loop.stop: one draft and at most two regenerations; else the analyst writes it
loop.why_not_simpler: the options and wording depend on the question in free text; a template cannot cover them

steps.what: Discuss options with the site or department manager

tasks.design: A certified Power BI semantic model on the AFAS extract holds actuals, budget and the allocation keys as versioned tables. A small Python job on the governed data platform runs standard cost and allocation analyses on request and writes an Excel workpaper. A bounded model step drafts an options memo whose numbers are checked against the workpaper.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each question needed a new Excel build because allocation keys and drivers lived in personal workbooks, not in one model.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes a governed model and analysis scripts cheap to build. Copilot in Power BI and LLM drafting can write commentary on a prepared model [S3].
tasks.still_hard: Agreeing allocation keys across sites and keeping the model in sync with the AFAS chart of accounts. Judgement on what a manager should do stays human [S1].
tasks.human_edge: Knowing the site, the manager and the trade-off, and saying no when the numbers do not support a plan.

ambition.what: Team leaders in warehouses and transport get a self-service cost view for their own cost centre, with the analyst handling only the questions it cannot answer.

tasks.altitude: The analyst answers fewer how-much questions and more what-should-we-do questions. They gain the right to set and change the allocation keys in the model, with Controller sign-off.

reach.task: Cost centre structure and allocation in AFAS
reach.learn: How allocation journals post, so the model matches the ledger.

evidence.claim: Finance executives found AI more useful than expected for budgeting and model building, least where human judgement is the work.
Copilot in Power BI summarises reports and writes DAX but needs a prepared semantic model and Fabric or Premium capacity.
Workpapers built in personal chatbots cannot be rebuilt for the auditor.

assumptions: The nightly AFAS extract includes cost centre, site and GL account per line.
Allocation keys can be agreed and written as tables.
unknowns: Whether Noordhaven has Fabric F2+ or Premium capacity.
How many advice requests arrive per month and from whom.
Whether allocation keys are documented today.
research_questions: Of the last 30 advice requests, how many could a standard analysis on the AFAS model have answered?
Can Controller and site managers agree on one set of allocation keys within a quarter?
Do managers act on a drafted options memo as readily as on an analyst-written one?

tasks.short: Review site and cost-centre budgets for trends in volume, labour and flex costs that change budget needs.

steps.what: Refresh extracts and build trend tables per site and cost centre
Spot deviations and likely drivers such as flex hours or fuel
Ask site managers and controllers about causes by mail
Write a trend note on budget needs for the Finance Director

loop.input: trend flags, driver figures and manager explanations in free text
loop.output: draft trend note citing the figures and the explanations used
loop.check: numbers checked by code against the trend tables; each claim links to a flag or an explanation
loop.stop: one draft, two retries; else analyst writes from the flags
loop.why_not_simpler: manager explanations arrive as free text and must be summarised and tied to figures

tasks.design: Trend tables become a Power BI page on the certified model with drivers (volume, shifts, flex hours, fuel) next to cost per site. Deterministic rules flag trends beyond set thresholds and send the cost-centre owner a Teams form for the cause. A bounded model step drafts the trend note from flags and answers.
tasks.previous_blocker: Driver data such as flex hours and volumes sat in agency portals and site sheets, not next to the ledger, so each review was rebuilt by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Cheap AI-assisted coding of extracts and rules, and LLM drafting of commentary on prepared data [S2][S3].
tasks.still_hard: Getting clean driver data from three agency portals and site systems. Faster trend output may invite more reports rather than better decisions [S1][S4].
tasks.human_edge: Telling a lasting trend from a one-off, and knowing which manager's explanation to trust.

ambition.what: Budget needs per site reviewed monthly instead of at the yearly budget round and mid-year review.

tasks.altitude: The analyst reads flags and causes instead of building tables. They decide which drivers and thresholds count and when a trend changes the forecast.

reach.task: Headcount and flex-hour reporting from AFAS
reach.learn: FTE and flex definitions, so labour trends use the same numbers as HR.

evidence.claim: OneStream describes agents that gather data, do variance arithmetic and draft commentary, while people decide which source wins.
Speed does not fix undefined drivers and makes existing errors harder to catch.
The most AI-mature finance teams spend more hours on executive reporting.

assumptions: Agency portals allow a regular export of hours per site.
Thresholds per driver can be set with the Controller.
unknowns: Export formats and access of the three agency portals.
Where volume data per site lives today.
Whether site managers will answer a Teams form.
research_questions: Can flex hours from all three agencies be loaded weekly without manual cleaning?
Over the past year, would threshold flags have caught the trends the team found by hand?
Do site managers answer a structured cause form within five working days?

tasks.short: Check monthly budget against actuals per cost centre and chase overruns to keep spending in control.

steps.what: Export AFAS ledger and agency invoices and tie them in Excel
Compute budget versus actual per cost centre and mark overruns
Investigate flagged lines in invoice and hours detail

loop.input: flagged GL lines with invoice descriptions and agency hour lines
loop.output: a proposed cause per line (timing, price, volume, misposting, one-off) with the source lines
loop.check: cause must cite source lines; amounts sum by code to the variance; analyst confirms each cause
loop.stop: one pass per flagged line; unclear lines go to the analyst unclassified
loop.why_not_simpler: invoice descriptions are free text in Dutch and vary per supplier and agency

steps.what: Mail cost-centre owners about overruns and track follow-up

tasks.design: The Excel sheet that ties AFAS and the agency portals becomes a scheduled Python job on the governed data platform that loads the ledger and agency invoices and hours, ties them and feeds a variance page in Power BI. A bounded model step proposes a cause for each flagged line, and a workflow sends approved overrun notices to cost-centre owners and tracks answers.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agency invoices and hours came from three portals in different formats, so tying them to the ledger was manual every month.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes portal parsers and tie-out rules quick to build; small model calls can read free-text invoice lines [S2].
tasks.still_hard: Portal formats change, and the ledger posting timing at month end makes variances noisy. 'A good guess isn't good enough' in finance, so causes need confirmation [S5].
tasks.human_edge: Deciding which overruns matter and pressing a manager to act without damaging the relationship.

ambition.what: Weekly flex-cost control per site during peak season instead of a monthly look after close.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends close week on causes and action, not tie-outs. They gain the right to set the overrun thresholds that trigger a notice.

reach.learn: Which invoice-hour mismatches are timing and which are real overspend.

evidence.claim: Agents can flag records that do not tie and do variance arithmetic; people decide which source wins.
Data quality is the top barrier to AI in finance (40.4%).
In payroll and finance, a good guess isn't good enough.

assumptions: AFAS GetConnectors or the nightly extract give GL lines with invoice reference.
The three agencies give invoice and hour files in a stable format.
unknowns: Whether agency portals offer API or only CSV/PDF.
How many lines get flagged in a typical month.
Who owns each cost centre in AFAS today.
research_questions: Can last year's twelve month-ends be rebuilt by the job with the same variances as the Excel sheet?
What share of flagged lines does the cause proposal get right in a back-test?
Does sending notices with causes shorten time to manager response?

tasks.short: Check managers' budget estimates for completeness, correct sums and conformance with budget rules and CAO rates.

steps.what: Collect budget templates from managers by mail and SharePoint
Check completeness, sums and account mapping
Check labour cost against CAO scales and budget policy

loop.input: manager free-text justifications and the budget policy text
loop.output: list of lines where the justification does not meet a policy rule, with the rule cited
loop.check: wage and headcount maths done by code; model findings must cite a policy paragraph; analyst confirms
loop.stop: one pass per budget; uncertain items marked for the analyst
loop.why_not_simpler: justifications are free text; rates and sums are coded, the policy fit is not

steps.what: Challenge outliers against history and agree changes with managers

tasks.design: Managers enter budgets in a simple input app (Power Apps or a small web form on the governed platform) that enforces the account list and cost centres, so the mail round disappears. Deterministic checks test completeness, sums, CAO wage scales and headcount against AFAS, and a bounded model step checks free-text justifications against the budget policy on SharePoint.
tasks.previous_blocker: Budgets arrived as free-form Excel files with changed layouts, so checks could not be coded once.
tasks.enabler_now: A structured input app and rule checks are cheap to build with AI coding; models can read justifications against a policy text.
tasks.still_hard: Getting managers to use the app, and keeping CAO tables current after each wage round. Headcount lines with named people are personal data under the AVG.
tasks.human_edge: Sensing padding or rollover budgets and challenging a manager on it face to face [S4].

ambition.what: A budget input app with instant feedback to site managers on errors and policy gaps before they submit.

tasks.altitude: The analyst no longer chases files or checks sums. They decide the budget rules and checks and spend the budget round on challenge conversations.

reach.task: Maintaining CAO wage scales and allowances
reach.learn: How scale steps and shift allowances drive labour cost per FTE.

evidence.claim: Rollover budgets and padding are not fixed by AI speed; encoded policies and defined drivers come first.
Budgeting showed the largest net gain from AI among finance tasks (+42).
Headcount plans with named people are personal data.

assumptions: A written budget policy exists on SharePoint.
CAO wage tables are available as data from AFAS or C&B.
unknowns: Whether named headcount is in the budget or only FTE per function.
Whether the works council sees the input app as a tool needing consent.
How many managers submit budgets each year.
research_questions: Which share of last year's review comments were completeness or arithmetic errors a rule could catch?
Will site managers accept an input app instead of their own Excel?
Can the budget policy be written as checkable rules with few exceptions?
